---
title: createCachedStore
description: Keep a Valtio store alive across Provider unmount/remount — in memory, keyed by name — so filters, pagination, and in-progress edits survive navigation without persisting to storage.
---

# `createCachedStore`

`createContextStore` creates a fresh proxy on `Provider` mount and throws it away on unmount. That is exactly right for a modal or a one-off form — but not for a table whose filters and pagination should still be there when the user navigates away and back.

`createCachedStore` is a **separate, opt-in** primitive that keeps the whole live proxy alive in an in-memory cache, keyed by a name you choose. Cache-hits return the **same** proxy object, so in-progress mutations survive unmount/remount within `gcTime`. `createContextStore` is unchanged.

The package ships a **ready-made default cache**: import `CacheProvider` and `createCachedStore` directly and you are done; no instance to create. This page uses the default cache throughout. If you need an isolated cache or several independent caches, see [Custom or multiple caches](#custom-or-multiple-caches) at the end.

The cache surface mirrors [`@ez-kit/zu-store`](../zu-store/store-cache) name-for-name — `createStoreCache` / `createCachedStore` / `CacheProvider` / `CacheScope` / `useCache` / `useCacheKeys`.

This page is the guide — what the pieces are for and how they behave. Every signature, prop and option is listed on [API reference](./cache/api).

## Keep-alive in action

Close the table (its `Provider` unmounts) and reopen it — the filter and page are exactly where you left them, because the proxy was kept alive in the cache.

## Quick start

Two steps: define a named store group, then mount the cache boundary once.

```tsx
import { CacheProvider, createCachedStore } from '@ez-kit/va-store'
import { proxy } from 'valtio'

type TableState = { filter: string; page: number }

// 1. Define a named store group against the default cache.
const usersTable = createCachedStore<TableState>(() => proxy<TableState>({ filter: 'all', page: 1 }), {
	name: 'users-table',
})

// 2. Mount the cache boundary once, high in the tree.
function App({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
	return <CacheProvider>{children}</CacheProvider>
}
```

Then mount the keyed `Provider` wherever the table lives. It survives unmount and is reused on remount:

```tsx
function UsersPage() {
	return (
		<usersTable.Provider id='users'>
			<UsersTable />
		</usersTable.Provider>
	)
}

function UsersTable() {
	const snap = usersTable.useSnapshot()
	const store = usersTable.useStore() // the raw mutable proxy — mutate directly
	return (
		<input
			value={snap.filter}
			onChange={(event) => {
				store.filter = event.target.value // survives navigating away and back
			}}
		/>
	)
}
```

`useSnapshot()`, `useStore()`, `Subscribe`, and `Store` behave exactly like [`createContextStore`](./create-context-store): read from the snapshot, mutate the proxy. There are no selectors — reading is `useSnapshot()`, writing is `useStore()`, and `Store` is the write-only slot that never subscribes.

## How it stays alive

Each `<Provider>` is counted as an observer. When the **last** one unmounts, the proxy is kept for `gcTime`, then evicted. Remount within that window and you get the same proxy back.

```tsx
// gcTime resolution (first match wins):
<usersTable.Provider id='users' />                 // cache default (5 min here)
<usersTable.Provider id='users' gcTime={30_000} /> // this entry: 30s after last unmount
<usersTable.Provider id='users' alwaysCache />     // never auto-evict
```

`gcTime` and `alwaysCache` are **birth-config**: they are fixed by the first mount that creates the entry. Later mounts attach to the existing proxy and ignore them.

### Opting one place out of keep-alive

`gcTime={0}` is the other end of the same dial: the entry is evicted as soon as its last observer leaves, so this one mounting point behaves like [`createContextStore`](./create-context-store) while the rest of the group keeps its state. The next mount creates a fresh proxy and `defaultValue` seeds it again, which is also the answer to "on this screen I want to start from the seed every time" — there is no separate reset-on-mount switch, and deliberately so: a flag that clears on mount would wipe the state under any _other_ `Provider` still observing the same key, while `gcTime` simply waits for the last one to leave.

```tsx
<usersTable.Provider
	id='draft'
	gcTime={0}
	defaultValue={{ filter: 'all' }}
/>
```

A handoff still survives: when one `Provider` unmounts and another on the same key mounts in the same commit — a route cross-fade, a re-parented subtree — the returning observer cancels the pending eviction.

Being birth-config, `gcTime={0}` only takes effect if this `Provider` is the one that **creates** the entry. If the same `(path, id)` is already live because another mounting point created it with the group's or cache's `gcTime`, the `0` is ignored — give the opted-out place its own `id` or `path`.

## `defaultValue` seeds once

`defaultValue` seeds the proxy **only when the key is first created**. On remount of a live entry it is ignored — that is the whole point of keep-alive. Type the factory's `init` parameter and read `init.defaultValue` to use it.

To open a page with pre-set state, drive it from the URL and seed from there, rather than mutating a cold store:

```tsx
<usersTable.Provider
	id='users'
	defaultValue={{ filter: searchParams.get('filter') ?? 'all' }}
/>
```

## Reading from anywhere

The group exposes two cross-tree reads at an address `({ path?, id })`. Neither ever **creates** an entry, and neither keeps one alive. Reads are addressed by the **absolute** `{ path, id }` — `path` defaults to `[]` (root) when omitted, never to the surrounding `Scope`.

### `getFromCache({ path, id })` — imperative

An imperative get-if-alive that returns the live proxy or `undefined`. Use it in event handlers or non-React code:

```tsx
function ResetButton() {
	return (
		<button
			onClick={() => {
				const live = usersTable.getFromCache({ id: 'users' })
				if (live) {
					live.filter = 'all'
					live.page = 1
				}
			}}
		>
			Reset
		</button>
	)
}
```

### `useFromCache({ path, id }, selector)` — reactive

Reactively read a cached entry from **anywhere** — even a badge that is not inside the table's `Provider`. The selector receives the entry's **snapshot**, or `undefined` when no entry is live, so the component re-renders only when the fields it actually reads change:

```tsx
function ActiveFilterBadge() {
	const filter = usersTable.useFromCache({ id: 'users' }, (snap) => snap?.filter ?? 'none')
	return <span>{filter}</span>
}
```

`useFromCache` is **passive** — it reflects the cache but does not keep the entry alive. Once the owning `Provider` unmounts and `gcTime` elapses, the entry is evicted and the reader's selector sees `undefined` again. Use `alwaysCache` if a reader must outlive its writer.

`remove({ path?, id })` drops one entry immediately (overriding `alwaysCache`).

## Inspecting and clearing

`useCache()` exposes the active cache (`keys(prefix?)`, `clear(prefix?)`). `useCacheKeys(prefix?)` is the reactive inspection hook — it re-renders only when cache **membership** changes (entries added or removed):

```tsx
import { useCache, useCacheKeys } from '@ez-kit/va-store'

function CacheBadge() {
	const records = useCacheKeys() // [{ path, name, id }, ...]
	return <span>{records.length} cached</span>
}
```

For a nested view of the same coordinates, compose `toTree(useCacheKeys(prefix))`.

## Namespacing with `Scope`

A cache entry's identity has three axes: a **`path`** (where in the app it lives), the **`name`** (the group name), and the **`id`** (which instance). `CacheScope` contributes inherited `path` segments to every descendant `Provider`, so a reusable component mounted on two pages never collides. Nested `Scope`s concatenate (outermost first); the `path` prop on a `Provider` is appended after the inherited scope. This works exactly as it does in [`@ez-kit/zu-store`](../zu-store/store-cache#namespacing-with-scope).

## Custom or multiple caches

The default cache covers the common "one cache per app" case. For an **isolated** cache, **several independent** caches, or a custom default `gcTime`, build your own with `createStoreCache()`; it returns the same surface as instance members instead of top-level exports:

```tsx
import { createStoreCache } from '@ez-kit/va-store'
import { proxy } from 'valtio'

const sessionCache = createStoreCache({ gcTime: 30_000 })
const draft = sessionCache.createCachedStore(() => proxy({ title: '' }), { name: 'draft' })

function App() {
	return <sessionCache.Provider>{/* … */}</sessionCache.Provider>
}
```

A store group is **bound to the cache that created it** — mount it under that cache's `Provider`.

## Cached **and** persisted

A capability like [`withPersist`](./persist) attaches to the proxy itself, inside the factory — so `createCachedStore` composes with it exactly the way `createContextStore` does: `cache.createCachedStore(() => withPersist(proxy({ … })), { name })`. A cached store can ALSO carry `withPersist` this way — kept alive in memory **and** mirrored to the URL or storage at once, under one `StoreProvider`. The lifetimes differ, and that is the point: the cache entry outlives any single `Provider` mount, so the capability attached to it does too. See [Persist → Cached stores](./persist/cache).
